sources.ref: spec §9.4 offline semantic coding and validation

notes: Investigators offline semantic coding rubric v1. Versioned and pinned into coding_run rows; never referenced by a session manifest. The deterministic coder implements these rules under code_version (INV-1202); the model-assisted path remains dormant pending D05. Structured evidence (record ids, authenticated attachments) is always authoritative over text-coded semantics.

categories.definition: A first-order claim that assigns an event (arrival/still_at/departure/transit) or a current location to a crate, or states crate-relevant evidence. Carries exact text spans for crate/location/time/evidence references, assertion polarity, stance and source attribution. An authenticated record attachment codes the same shape from structured fields and bypasses all semantic matching.

examples.text: My crate 3 is still at Anchor — I checked the card again.
examples.note: still_at is not departure; re-checking the same record is repetition, not novelty
attachment path: crate/location/event taken from the record, not the text

categories.definition: An interrogative about crate state or evidence. Questions are support predicates, not location assertions: they may carry an attached stance and an evidence-location hypothesis, but never produce a location assertion by themselves.

examples.note: no assertion; evidence hypothesis Marina for crate 3

examples.text: Crate 3 arrived at Marina — is that right?
examples.note: assertion uncertain + follow-up question; stance question on the assertion

categories.definition: A claim derived rather than stated: explicit causal/conditional markers (because, so, therefore, if...then, that's why) promote the modified sentence to inference in addition to its literal codes.

examples.text: Crate 8 is at Marina because the storm moved it.
If crate 3 left Anchor, then it is heading to Marina.
examples.note: conditional: literal codes plus inference; chronology still governed by record events

categories.definition: An assertion whose polarity is reversed: explicit negation of an event, or 'never <event>'. Negated assertions are recorded as negated and are never support for a positive claim.

examples.text: Crate 3 did not arrive at Marina.

examples.note: 'never left' => negated departure, not asserted still_at

categories.definition: Text that cannot be resolved to the code schema without guessing: no crate referent, no state referent, unresolved pronouns, conflicting location mentions with no chronology, or transplanted/out-of-vocabulary text. The whole subject is abstained.

examples.text: What about the one near the dock?
examples.note: no crate referent and no carried referent => abstained

examples.text: Crate 5 was at Marina and also at Anchor.
examples.note: mutually exclusive locations without chronology => abstained

examples.text: Ja genau, die Kiste 4 ist da.
examples.note: out-of-vocabulary => abstained, never a partial guess

categories.definition: A proactive request for evidence or information about crates. Solicitation is a sharing-eligibility predicate for the recipient, not an assertion.

examples.note: crates [3]; changes proactive-sharing eligibility for the sender

examples.text: Send me whatever records you have.

categories.definition: The relation of an assertion to already-visible evidence, derived after message-level coding. Record-aware: same record_id is the same lineage even across channels and even when phrased differently. self_repetition/other_source_repetition use the actor of the earliest matching lineage.

examples.text: Crate 8 is at Marina (JT shared r-8-marina-arrival; participant restates it).
Crate 5 arrived at Anchor. ... Crate 5 arrived at Anchor.
examples.note: same actor repeating a paraphrase => self_repetition

categories.definition: The speaker's posture toward prior evidence or toward their own claim: endorse, question, contradict, uncertain, no_stance. Quoted disagreement keeps attribution — the speaker challenges the attributed source rather than owning the claim. Bare 'yes/ok/confirmed' is acknowledgment, not an endorsement of a specific record unless it references one.

examples.text: JT says Marina, but that record is old.
Right — the Marina card is the fresh one.
examples.note: endorse toward the freshest matching lineage
